title: Instability of Markov chains under infinitesimal coherent dissipation
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Yijian Zou, Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract: Under local Lindbladian evolution, the growth of conditional mutual information and its associated Markov length scale is not limited by Lieb-Robinson bounds, yet it has been unclear how quickly the Markov length can increase. We show that an arbitrarily short, strictly local Lindbladian can generate infinite Markov length from a product state. We also construct strictly local Lindbladians that converge rapidly to steady states with algebraically decaying conditional mutual information. Despite their long-range conditional correlations, the states we construct are local reversibly connected to a product state by sublinear depth circuits. Thus infinite Markov length does not imply slow relaxation nor obstruct phase stability when suitably defined.
summary: This theoretical paper examines how local dissipation affects the Markov length of quantum systems, using CMI as the primary diagnostic tool. The authors demonstrate that even when dynamics are rapidly relaxing, the system can maintain infinite Markov length. This suggests that the concept of finite Markov length is fragile and easily destroyed by weak local noise.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability of finite Markov length in quantum systems undergoing weak, local dissipative perturbations.
main_result: The authors show that infinite Markov length can be generated by arbitrarily short, strictly local Lindbladians, implying that finite Markov length is not robust against weak local dissipation.
method: The analysis heavily relies on calculating the Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) for both free-fermion and constructed spin systems.
model_or_system: The models include free fermion chains evolving under local Lindbladian dissipation, which is mapped to a strictly local spin Lindbladian using auxiliary fermions.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), Markov Length, and the decay rate of CMI.
important_parameters: Dissipation strength (Lindbladian parameters $p$), buffer width ($B$), and time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The initial analysis uses the free-fermion structure for tractability; the spin construction requires introducing auxiliary fermions to maintain locality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the algebraic decay of CMI for intermediate states at finite time, and the surface code diagnostics show how logical distance and matching probability evolve with code distance and time.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing free-fermion CMI decay to constructing an equivalent spin Lindbladian. It then analyzes the steady-state CMI decay and concludes by discussing the instability of local reversibility under weak dissipation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the stability of quantum correlations (Markov length) under realistic, dissipative environments, which is crucial for understanding quantum computation and thermalization in many-body systems.
